summary:
I could not refute the record's main runtime claims. The model does not fit in VRAM in any format, so vLLM is not viable on this GPU. llama.cpp with the ggml-org Q4_0 GGUF and --n-cpu-moe 16 is the realistic way to run it, and should give OpenCode working Qwen3-Coder-XML tool calls with 128K or more of context.

Re-checked live and confirmed:
- Weight sizes from the HF API: BF16 61.31 GiB, NVFP4 20.08 GiB, W4A16 16.60 GiB, ggml-org Q4_0 18,898,091,584 B (17.60 GiB), Ollama :latest blob 25,430,738,944 B.
- config.json: 6 attention layers at 5, 12, 19, 26, 33, 42, 23 mamba, 23 moe, 2 KV heads, head_dim 128, max_position_embeddings 262144. That gives 6144 B/token of BF16 KV.
- vLLM v0.33.0: registry line 186, the qwen3_coder and nemotron_v3 parsers, the cpu_offload_params setting and the recipe (vram_minimum_gb 18) all exist.
- llama.cpp b12418: LLM_ARCH_NEMOTRON_H_MOE and the Qwen3-Coder chat handler (line 1420) exist. --n-cpu-moe counts blocks, and blocks 0 to 15 hold 7 MoE layers.

Corrections:
1. The params field says non-expert weights are about 0.9B. Config arithmetic gives about 2.19B, which matches the 2.20 GiB of Q8_0 non-expert tensors in the GGUF.
2. --moe-cache-mib is a GPU-side cache for experts held on the CPU, not a host-memory cache.
3. The vLLM offload sketch is worse than 'untested'. Issue #66264 reports that on v0.33.0 with NVFP4 and Marlin on sm_120, repacked expert tensors fall back onto the GPU despite --cpu-offload-params experts, and loading runs out of memory.
4. Two GGUF problems were fixed upstream: zero KV-head metadata (#27718, fixed in a re-upload on 2026-08-26) and a wrong pre-tokenizer (#30894). b12418 now maps pixtral to tekken, so use a current build and the current file.

The llama.cpp fit is tight: about 15.2 of 15.92 GiB, and the overhead figures are assumptions. Use --fit on, or move one or two more MoE layers to RAM.

verdicts.claim: Checkpoint sizes: BF16 61.31 GiB (65.83 GB), NVIDIA NVFP4 20.08 GiB (21.56 GB), useful-quants W4A16 16.60 GiB, ggml-org Q4_0 17.60 GiB (18.90 GB) with the MTP head split out, bartowski Q4_K_M 25.48 GB
verdicts.correction: The size is right but the label is not: the ggml-org mtp Q4_0 file is 1,155,907,520 B (1.08 GiB / 1.16 GB). Also, ggml-org did have a Q4_K_M and deleted it on 2026-08-14 (commit 'Delete files ...Q4_K_M.gguf'). That explains the stale :Q4_K_M in NVIDIA's card.

verdicts.claim: Architecture: 52 layers (23 mamba, 23 moe, 6 attention at 5/12/19/26/33/42), 2 KV heads, head_dim 128, max_position_embeddings 262144, 128 experts top-6, shared expert 3712

verdicts.correction: From config: embedding plus untied output 0.70B, shared experts 0.46B, mamba 0.89B, attention 0.14B. That is about 2.19B non-expert parameters. At Q8_0 this is 2.17 GiB, which matches the 2.20 GiB non-expert share of the GGUF (tie_word_embeddings false). Routed experts are 29.37B, about 15.39 GiB at Q4_0.

verdicts.claim: KV bytes per token 6144 BF16 / 3072 FP8; Mamba state about 47 MiB per sequence
verdicts.correction: 2 x 6 x 2 x 128 x 2 = 6144 B. The SSM state is 23 x 64 x 64 x 128 x 4 B = 46 MiB, plus a small conv state (fp32, about 1.6 MiB in total).

verdicts.claim: vLLM: no checkpoint fits the 14.65 GiB budget (NVFP4 20.08, W4A16 16.60), fits=no
verdicts.correction: NVFP4: 14.65 - 20.08 - 1.2 = -6.63 GiB. W4A16: 14.65 - 16.60 - 1.2 = -3.15 GiB. Both are negative. The recipe states vram_minimum_gb 18 for NVFP4.

verdicts.claim: vLLM fallback sketch: NVFP4 + --moe-backend marlin + --cpu-offload-gb 8 --cpu-offload-params experts leaves 12.08 GiB on GPU and a 1.17 GiB KV pool
verdicts.correction: Open issue #66264 (2026-11-07) was filed against vLLM 0.33.0 on sm_120 with exactly NVFP4 + marlin + --cpu-offload-params experts. replace_parameter keeps the UVA marker but rebinds .data to a GPU tensor, so on 0.33.0 'every repacked expert tensor leaks' back to the GPU, and process_weights_after_loading runs out of memory. Expect this configuration to OOM at load on v0.33.0. Open issue #52225 (Xid 13 on SM120 with this model) adds further risk.

verdicts.claim: vLLM v0.33.0 registers NemotronHForCausalLM (registry.py line 186) and NemotronHMTPModel; parsers qwen3_coder and nemotron_v3 exist
llama.cpp b12418 supports nemotron_h_moe and routes the template to the Qwen3-Coder tool-call handler
verdicts.correction: llama-arch.cpp line 105 maps LLM_ARCH_NEMOTRON_H_MOE to nemotron_h_moe, and src/models/nemotron-h-moe.cpp exists. In chat.cpp, line 1420 has the comment 'Qwen3-Coder XML tool calls, also used by Nemotron Nano 3, Qwen3.5...' and line 1427 returns common_chat_params_init_qwen3_coder.

There were relevant issues, now closed. #27718: the ggml-org Q4_0 had all-zero KV-head metadata, so attention blocks loaded as SSM. It closed 2026-08-26, the day ggml-org re-uploaded the files. #30894: Nemotron 3/3.5 GGUFs were tagged 'pixtral' and got the Llama3 pre-tokenizer. b12418 llama-vocab.cpp line 2624 now treats pixtral as tekken. #27717: --n-cpu-moe below a threshold crashed MTP draft loading. It was closed not_planned, so it is still a risk only if you load the MTP file. Use a current build and the current file, and do not load the mtp-*.gguf.

verdicts.claim: llama.cpp v1.0.0 (2026-11-13) is the latest stable release and adds a host-memory MoE expert cache (--moe-cache-mib)
verdicts.correction: The release part holds: v1.0.0 is releases/latest, not a prerelease, published 2026-11-13T10:20:19Z. The cache description is wrong. arg.cpp at b12418 says '--moe-cache-mib: GPU cache size in MiB for the MoE experts kept in the CPU' (default 0, disabled). It is a VRAM cache, so any MiB given to it reduce the KV and weight budget.

verdicts.claim: llama.cpp plan: Q4_0, --n-cpu-moe 16 moves 7 MoE layers (4.68 GiB) to RAM, about 15.2 GiB VRAM at 131072 f16 KV, about 5.5 GiB RAM
verdicts.correction: --n-cpu-moe is documented as 'keep the MoE weights of the first N layers in the CPU'. The MoE blocks below 16 are 1, 3, 6, 8, 10, 13 and 15, so 7 layers x 0.669 GiB = 4.68 GiB. The GPU estimate is 2.20 + 10.70 + 0.75 KV + 0.05 state + about 1.4 overhead + 0.11 idle = about 15.2 GiB out of 15.92 GiB. That is tight, and the compute buffer and CUDA context figures are assumptions (inferred). Fall back to --fit on, or to --n-cpu-moe 18 to 20.
The registry manifest model layer is 25,430,738,944 B. On 16 GB that means about 10 GB offloaded to CPU, so it will be slower than the llama.cpp Q4_0 route.

verdicts.claim: Verdict: serves OpenCode with working tool calls and at least 64k context on this machine via llama.cpp (Q4_0, partial expert offload); not via vLLM
verdicts.correction: Every element that can be checked from sources holds: the architecture is supported, the tool handler is present, KV costs only 6 KiB/token, and the 131072 to 262144 context and the memory split are consistent. It has not been run on this machine or any 16 GB card, so leave it 'inferred'. The 60 to 110 tok/s estimate slightly overcounts bytes read per token, because only one embedding row is read per token, which makes it conservative. vLLM is not realistic on v0.33.0 because of #66264.
